title: Debug build works. Release build (-DNDEBUG) reads garbage. Tap the bug.
explain: With -DNDEBUG, assert() is removed completely. The call to uart_read() disappears too, so b is never written. Never put code with side effects inside assert(). Run the call first, then assert on the result.

title: send() sends 0 bytes. No crash, no error. Tap the bug.
explain: reserve() only allocates memory. The size stays 0. memcpy writes 64 bytes into elements that do not exist yet, which is undefined behavior, and buf.size() is still 0. Use resize(64), or construct the vector with the size.

title: A short radio frame resets the MCU. Tap the bug.
explain: frame comes from the air, so its length is not trusted. &frame[..4] panics when the frame has fewer than 4 bytes. A panic in firmware usually means a reset. Check the length and drop bad frames. first_chunk::<4>() does both in one step.

pr.title: Check frame header size at compile time
pr.author: senior-dev
pr.body: The header must match the wire format. Fail the build if the size changes.

explain: Good change. 1 + 1 + 2 + 4 = 8 bytes, so the check passes today. If someone adds a field or removes packed, the build fails at once and not on the bus. Not every PR has a bug: approve good code fast.

pr.title: Enable UART IRQ first, do not miss the first byte
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: The bootloader leaves RXNEIE on. Enable the NVIC first so the first byte is not lost.

explain: RXNEIE is already on, so the ISR can fire right after NVIC_EnableIRQ. At that moment rx_cb is still NULL, and the ISR calls a NULL pointer: HardFault. Set up all state first, enable the IRQ last. Also guard the pointer, and always read DR.

pr.title: Replace static mut READY with AtomicBool
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: static mut bool is unsafe. AtomicBool is safe and Relaxed is the fastest.

explain: The flag is atomic, but SAMPLE is a normal variable. Relaxed gives no order between the two, so the compiler may move the write to SAMPLE after the flag store. Use Release when you set the flag and Acquire when you read it. Then the sample is published before the flag.

title: What does this print?
explain: The left side is 0 > 0, which is false, and i becomes 1. && stops there, so the right side never runs and i stays 1. There is a sequence point after the left operand, so it is not UB. Careful: a function call on the right side of && can be skipped too.

title: What does this print?
explain: saturating_sub stops at 0. wrapping_sub goes around: 5 - 8 = 65533 for u16. checked_sub gives None when the result would be below 0. Pick the one that fits: wrapping for tick counters, checked when an underflow is an error.

title: The SPI flash sometimes has wrong data after a reset. CS is a normal GPIO. What do you add?
options: 10 kΩ pull-up from CS to VCC
10 kΩ pull-down from CS to GND
explain: CS is active low. During reset and boot the MCU pin is a floating input, so the flash can see random CS pulses and take clock edges as commands. A pull-up keeps CS high (chip not selected) until the firmware drives the pin.

title: Enabling an interrupt: 4 rules for the order
bullets: First set up everything the ISR uses: buffers, indexes, callbacks, clocks.
Clear old pending flags before you enable the IRQ, or you get a ghost interrupt at once.
Enable the peripheral interrupt bit, then the NVIC line last.
In the ISR, always clear or read the source flag, even when the callback is NULL.
